Panic has gripped the remote frontier villages of India’s border with China, where tribal communities say they are being pushed back from their ancestral yak-grazing and hunting landsdue to a rapidly growing threat – the advancing Chinese Army.

Satellite images accessed by The Independent show a rapid expansion of infrastructure at multiple sites along and near the disputed India-China frontier in Arunachal Pradesh, including new buildings, roads, as well as helipads.

The imagery offers a rare visual record of the changing landscape along one of the most inaccessible sections of the frontier in the Himalayas, where competing territorial claims and the difficulty of maintaining a permanent Indian presence have left communities living close to the border increasingly anxious.

Takok Mra spoke to The Independent on the phone from his remote village around 20km from the border in India’s Arunachal Pradesh, which China claims in its entirety and calls Zangnan or Southern Tibet. He said he was willing to fight the Chinese army – if it comes to that.

"The Chinese are currently encroaching on our ancestral land. We eat, survive and run our livelihoods from here, and it is our land. They have already entered very far inside Indian territory," Mra says. "I cannot say exactly how many kilometres they have taken, but they have taken a lot.”

With China’s Xi Jinping travelling to India to meet with his counterpart Narendra Modi this weekend, part of the largest Chinese delegation to travel to India in years, both countries’ governments have sought to play down any tensions at the border, denying there is an active standoff akin to the skirmishes that cost at least 20 Indian soldiers’ lives back in 2020.

But the satellite images and testimony from border villages paint a different picture, one of sustained Chinese advances and infrastructure development in contested territory that remains part of talks between the two countries’ diplomatic and military officials.

In the satellite images provided by Vantor, analysts note recent construction and infrastructure changes at multiple sites in the Upper Subansiri Valley, where Mra’s village of Gelemo is located.

Two sites near Zhari town in the north of Lhunze County in Tibet, on the Chinese-held side of the frontier, show the clearest activity, according to Janes, a global open-source intelligence company.

“The satellite imagery confirms there is recent construction in the areas of interest,” say analysts at Janes, adding that when the satellite imagery is overlaid with both India's and China's competing interpretations of the border, the imagery shows that some of this infrastructure sits within territory claimed by both countries, placing it squarely inside the disputed zone.

open image in gallery Satellite image shows Zhari town and a large village to its north in Lhunze County, Tibet, on 22 October 2022 ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

open image in gallery Satellite image shows Zhari town and a large village to its north in Lhunze County, Tibet, on 4 March 2026. The images show the expansion of Zhari town and surrounding infrastructure, with new buildings, roads and cleared areas visible across the valley ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

At one location south of the town, construction that began in early 2019 – with the first visible structures appearing by August that year – is still ongoing. The site shows flattened land, construction while engineering vehicles are present, and a cement plant being installed. The possibility of it being for military use cannot be ruled out, analysts told The Independent.

A separate construction site inside the town itself has, in the analysts' assessment, "roughly an even chance" of being a military facility.

Nearby, a stretch of road has been widened and its grade reduced – improvements that make it easier to move heavy equipment and are often a precursor to paving the road for year-round use.

open image in gallery Satellite imagery shows a small village in southern Zhari town, Lhunze, Tibet, on 22 October 2022 ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

open image in gallery Satellite imagery shows a small village in southern Zhari town, Lhunze, Tibet, on 4 March 2026 ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

South of Luhnze, the imagery shows a new helipad built to replace two smaller ones, along with another new helipad further south.

The latest Vantor image from August 2026 shows at least one structure now has a roof, indicating construction is still underway. Analysts assess the site is likely military in nature, citing the layout, the presence of vehicles matching military patterns, and an adjoining training area. A new road connecting to the town was also built between February and May 2026.

open image in gallery A comparison of satellite imagery shows changes and new development in Raorang in Tibet between 2 November 2022 and January 2026. Pictures show some construction at several further sites with possible military characteristics, including one additional training area ( Satellite image ©2026 Vantor )

A road near the town was also constructed between February and May 2026.

The allegations surface at a delicate moment in Sino-India relations. Xi’s visit to Delhi for the Brics summit is his first trip to India since the 2020 border skirmish in the Galwan Valley that saw relations between the two nuclear-powered nations plummet to their worst level in decades. Xi is expected to travel with a delegation of around 400 officials.

Amid growing clamour among locals over Chinese activity, two independent fact-finding groups travelled to Gelemo and Taksing – remote, high-altitude villages roughly 15-20km from the Sino-India border in the eastern Himalayas – to assess the situation on the ground.

Tadak Pakba, president of the All Tagin Students' Union (ATSU), led a group of eight people to Gelemo and Taksing, gathering reports directly from local residents, tribal communities and military porters. ATSU represents the Tagin Indigenous community of Arunachal Pradesh.

open image in gallery Chinese vehicles carring traders enter Indian territory after crossing the China-India border at the 15 000-feet (4545-metre) Nathu La Pass, in India's northeastern state of Sikkim on May 19 ,2008 ( AFP/Getty )

Pakba says the way the alleged Chinese incursion is happening there now “has not been seen before”.

“There is not only panic in border villages, but this is the fact of reality on the ground. The Indian Army is going back and the Chinese army is coming forward,” he says.

Between 11 and 13 August, local leader Pakba and his team conducted a three-day field investigation and reported Chinese encroachment at several positions normally patrolled by the Indian Army.

These include remote hunting and yak-grazing grounds that for years have been accessible to Indian villagers. "Villagers are currently forbidden from accessing these areas... this has caused panic among locals, leading some to move away from the border areas," Pakba says.

“This is all very recent – happening since June this year,” he adds.

open image in gallery An overview of Gelemo, a remote border village located in the Upper Subansiri district of Arunachal Pradesh, India ( Supplied )

The fact-finding report, submitted to the deputy commissioner of Upper Subansiri and the chief minister's office and seen by The Independent, demands "immediate intervention" into "reported presence and activities of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA)" in the Taksing-Gelemo frontier region.

It should be treated as a matter of "grave strategic and national importance," not an "ordinary developmental issue", the report says.

The issue was first raised by the Nah Welfare Society (NWS), a local tribal body representing the Nah Indigenous community that migrated from Tibet and settled in Upper Subansiri district generations ago.

It submitted a memorandum to the deputy commissioner of Upper Subansiri, claiming that the PLA has established roads, bridges and military camps in several locations traditionally used by local communities for grazing, hunting and the collection of forest produce.

"The intention and speed of the present activities of the Chinese PLA at Taksing are very alarming. We are losing our land inch by inch day by day," it added.

For Mra, the alleged loss of access to traditional land along India's frontier with China is not an abstract territorial dispute – it is a personal loss. His family has held this ancestral land since the 1962 India-China war.

open image in gallery Takok Mra, a resident of Gelemo in Arunachal Pradesh, where concerns of Chinese incursion have been emerging ( Supplied )

"I am a true patriot. Give us weapons to save our country and our land," says the 38-year-old.

Tribal communities who hunt and graze in the Himalayan forests are more than just passive bystanders in the border conflict, and will pass information to the Indian Army about troop movements in the disputed regions. Mra says that as early as June, they informed the army about the presence of Chinese troops – after which the army became more active in the area.

Expressing frustration over the lack of basic amenities such as electricity, roads, healthcare and schools in his village, Mra contrasts this with the aggressive Chinese infrastructure development near the border.

"When we reach our village Gelemo, we feel completely cut off from the world. Due to lack of basic facilities, our local people move to the district to earn a living, and that is why the border is slowly becoming empty," he says, suggesting that this movement of people from remote areas is in part allowing the Chinese army to advance.

A second fact-finding mission was led by the People's Party of Arunachal Pradesh (PPA) – part of a regional bloc allied with India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) – which sent a four-member team to the border areas.

Kapa Bengia, chief advisor to PPA and a former minister in the state, was part of the group which visited Taksing, Galemo, and Maza, one of the villages closest to the border.

Bengia says: “They (Chinese Army) are already advancing, and our patrolling group is not allowed to move towards our own land.”

The Nanga Pahar, a strategic border area in the remote Taksing circle used by the Nah and other tribal communities, have been declared a strictly prohibited zone for local residents, the report said.

The Indian Army has broadly dismissed reports of a Chinese incursion into disputed territory as "incorrect and without any basis."

However, India's foreign ministry was less direct in its response, describing border issues as a "more serious" part of maintaining peaceful relations between the two countries.

Indian government spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: “We have also stated that the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties.”

China also issued a statement, though it neither confirmed nor denied fresh border tensions.

"The China-India border situation is generally stable at the moment," said Guo Jiakun, a foreign ministry spokesperson in Beijing.

The closest the Indian side has come to confirming any concerns came in Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Kandhu's account of a meeting with defence minister Rajnath Singh. Singh, he said, was "very concerned and proactive about this issue" and will "certainly provide the necessary infrastructural support" in the coming days.

open image in gallery A 2023 shows a Buddhist temple on the outskirts of Dirang in India's Arunachal Pradesh state ( AFP/Getty )

Ajay Murtem, a local public leader in Arunachal Pradesh and a native of Upper Subansiri district, says: "New battle lines between China and India will be drawn in Upper Subansiri district if the Indian government does not stop China's expansion into Taksing, Maja, Gelemo and the Shreechu valley."

Murtem says the Tagin tribe – one of Arunachal Pradesh's major Indigenous communities – and its subclan Nah community hold ceremonial rituals at Potrang Lake, just an hour from Taksing. In recent days, however, tribal people have been stopped by the Chinese army from visiting the traditionally sacred Buddhist worship site.

“We are all patriots. The people living along the international frontier are not merely inhabitants of remote villages. They are also the eyes and ears of the nation along the border.”

What is happening in Arunachal Pradesh is part of China's "salami slicing" strategy, says Srikanth Kondapalli, a professor of China studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi, referring to a process in which small, incremental moves are made and consolidated over time rather than through one major incursion.

"First, the Chinese release some yaks and wait for the Indian army's response. If it's absent for months, they install a small shed, then convert it into a permanent structure – and when they face no resistance, they build a small army company," he explains, calling it a "grey zone" where the McMahon Line – the de facto boundary between India's Arunachal Pradesh state and Tibet – is not legally defined.

open image in gallery File: Chinese President Xi Jinping and India Prime Minister Narendra Modi meet on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia October 23, 2024 ( Reuters )

The Indian government has made some efforts to launch its own version of Beijing’s frontier villages, which China has succeeded in populating and refers to has Xiaokang or “well-off societies”, thereby bolstering its territorial claims.

India’s version – the Vibrant Village Programme – “has not been successful”, says Kondapalli, because “it needs a lot of ecosystem [building]”. “While China has constructed roughly 100 model villages in Longju, and from there they began expanding into Indian-claimed areas in Arunachal.”

India's inability to regularly reach the de facto border or “line of actual control”, he says, gives China an opening to pursue its salami-slicing strategy.

open image in gallery India and China border in Sikkim ( AFP/Getty )

"Until you prepare your infrastructure and consolidate your position on the line of actual control, there is simply no way that you can have any leverage. The Chinese can come up to the line of actual control within 24 hours. They began road construction in the 1980s. We just woke up."

The border issue is a major talking point in India, and domestic audiences will be watching closely for any developments during the summit this weekend. But with any direct press interactions by Xi and Modi highly unlikely, Kondapalli says there is a relatively low chance of the matter being raised by either side. With China due to take over as Brics host next year, both countries are heavily invested in presenting this year’s talks as a success.

Leaders of the BRICS nations were meeting in New Delhi on Saturday for a summit focused on trade, investment and global conflicts, as the bloc seeks a bigger role in shaping the global agenda for emerging and developing countries.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is hosting Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and counterparts from the other eight BRICS members. The summit comes as wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, along with rising U.S.-China tensions, test the bloc’s ability to find common ground among countries with competing geopolitical interests.

Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed around the summit venue and other parts of New Delhi, with traffic restrictions and diversions in place.

BRICS was founded in 2006 by Brazil, Russia, India and China, with South Africa joining in 2010. It has since expanded to 11 members, representing about half the world’s population and a significant share of global economic output. The group has increasingly called for greater representation for developing countries in global institutions.

The leaders are expected to discuss economic cooperation, energy, food security, technology, supply chains and reforms to global institutions. Reducing reliance on the U.S. dollar will also be a priority, with members promoting greater use of their own currencies in trade and payments as well as pushing for alternatives to Western-dominated financial institutions.

For India, the summit highlights its effort to maintain strategic ties with Russia and Iran while deepening relations with the U.S. and Europe. New Delhi has sought to balance its longstanding partnerships with Moscow and Tehran with efforts to expand economic, defense and technology ties with Washington and other Western nations.

India has maintained close ties with both Moscow and Tehran despite the war in Ukraine and tensions between Iran and the U.S., while calling for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve conflicts. Modi met Putin and Pezeshkian separately in New Delhi on Friday ahead of the summit.

The summit comes as Iran, a member of the expanded BRICS group, is directly involved in the war in the Middle East, putting the bloc’s unity under pressure as its members navigate differing positions on the conflict and relations with the U.S.

A key test for India will be whether it can secure a joint statement from leaders at the summit. Those divisions were evident in May, when BRICS foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement over the Iran war, forcing India to issue a chair’s summary instead.

News.title: Razaullah’s incredible hitting scrambles England’s minds
News.content:
England will look to complete the series whitewash as they hold a commanding position coming into day three of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston in what could be the final day of the English Test summer.

England finished up their first innings on 453 on day two, with a mammoth 320-run lead over Pakistan. Five England batsmen passed the fifty mark; Emilio Gay, Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith and Ollie Robinson, but none went on to convert those half centuries into hundreds. It means that Ben Duckett’s century against New Zealand at Trent Bridge back in June will be the only England Test hundred of the summer, the first time that has happened in a six-Test summer. England managed 21 half centuries over the course of the summer, so it works out as 4.76% conversion rate.

Having seen England pile on the runs, Pakistan then lost a wicket with the first ball of their second innings, with Saim Ayub making a pair to sum up a miserable return to their Test side for the opener having been jettisoned in as part of wholesale changes for the visitors. Abdullah Shafique followed three balls later, with Robinson taking both wickets as his fine summer continued. Robinson now has 28 wickets across four Tests this summer at a staggering average of 7.75. Joe Root made history yesterday, taking his 220th catch, the most by an outfielder in Test history. Rain though prevented England the opportunity of potentially wrapping up a two-day finish in a Test in this country for the first time since 2000.

Pakistan will resume on 52/2, still 268 runs behind England, with Azan Awais resuming on 29 not out and will be joined by Shan Masood, who is on 21. Pakistan are yet to reach 200 or bat more than 51 overs in this series so the series whitewash may not be a million miles away. Will we see any rare Pakistan resistance in this series or will England’s seamers dominate again? Play on day three from Edgbaston is set to get under at 11am and it could be the final day of not just the series but the English Test summer.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Badenoch must scrap triple lock, says senior Tory MP | Politician urges Conservatives to ‘slaughter some sacred cows’ to stabilise the public finances

2) | Michael O’Leary demands sacking of ‘incompetent’ air traffic control chief | Ryanair boss urges Transport Secretary to dismiss Martin Rolfe after IT meltdown grounds passengers

3) | Guardian staff threaten walkout over pay as paper hails record revenues | Journalists’ union will ballot members over strike in protest against company’s offer

4) | Hotel bosses criticise Burnham’s fresh assault on hospitality | Prime Minister gives mayors power for unlimited levy on stays in blow for pubs and families

5) | Iceland to become first British supermarket to open in Falklands | New shop will begin trading before Christmas despite rising tensions with Argentina over islands

What happened overnight

Oil prices remained at their highest level since May as tensions flared in the Middle East.

Brent crude was above $105 a barrel after after Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s keyport of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8pc to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8pc to 3,862.73.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2pc to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7pc, while India’s Sensex declined 1pc.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6pc in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6pc, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7pc.

News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: ‘All I see are dead bodies’: The survivors of Syria’s chemical massacres
News.content:
“Unfortunately, I am still alive,” says Mohammed Suliaiman Abo Alkair, his green eyes heavy and distant.

The 38-year-old steps from his living room onto the roof and gestures towards a cluster of trees – a lone patch of green in a sea of grey rubble. It was there, at two in the morning 13 years ago that the whistle of a rocket ended not in an explosion but a thud.

For a moment, there was relief; the feeling of being spared. But then came a cloud of the nerve agent sarin.

Almost everyone around Mohammed died. His family and one small boy in a neighbouring house were the only ones to survive.

That August night, as Damascus slept, forces loyal to the Syrian President Bashar al-Assad launched eight sarin-filled rockets at the opposition-held districts of Zamalka, Ein Tarma and Jobar. The US government estimated that 1,429 people were killed, including 426 children. Other estimates put the number at 1729.

For more than a decade, nobody was held to account. Mr Assad denied the attack, shielded those responsible and later used sarin again – at Khan Sheikhoun in 2017, and in at least ten further attacks documented by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Only after Mr Assad fled Syria in December 2024 did the prospect of justice emerge. Investigators for Syria’s new government have since uncovered previously undeclared chemical-munitions caches, and the authorities have detained 18 suspects. None has yet been tried or punished.

But as attention turns at last to justice, the survivors remain invisible, absent from the reckoning. For now at least they remain largely invisible.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs are frustrated to be left in the dark over Man City charges – and it could cost them £100m
Sports.content:
THERE is one subject which makes Premier League executives suddenly become very, very careful with their words — Manchester City.

Ask a chief executive what they think of the 130 financial breaches brought against City and you get the same answer: “I can’t comment.”



Ask when they think the verdict will come: “I can’t comment.”

It is almost as if somebody has handed every Prem chief executive the same script. But privately, of course, people talk.



The biggest frustration among the other 19 clubs is not simply that the case has taken so long, or it has cost so much money.

It is that they have almost no idea what is actually happening.



The Premier League have published the charges. But the evidence behind them is not public. Nor is City’s detailed defence.

So the clubs are effectively being asked to wait patiently for a verdict in a case whose workings they cannot see.

Football hates a vacuum. When there is no information, speculation takes over.

The Premier League formally announced the charges in February 2023, after a four-year probe.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Is the case taking so long because the evidence is so complicated? Are the three members of the independent commission divided?

Have they reached conclusions on some charges but not others?

Or have they actually reached a verdict and are simply taking enormous care to make the judgment legally watertight so that it cannot be challenged?

Nobody outside that room knows.

And that, ironically, is why there is so much speculation.



The allegations are hardly trivial.

At their heart is the Prem’s claim City deliberately misrepresented aspects of their finances and remuneration, potentially allowing them to comply with financial rules when, the League says, they should not have.

There are allegations concerning sponsorship income, remuneration connected to Roberto Mancini through an Abu Dhabi company, and player image-rights deals.

City deny wrongdoing and are entitled to defend themselves.

Now Mauricio Pochettino has raised another uncomfortable question, saying Tottenham should be awarded the 2017 title after Chelsea were punished for historic breaches involving agent payments.



I understand his argument. If clubs break the rules, there has to be a consequence. Otherwise rules are little more than suggestions. But I am not convinced you can simply hand the title to the team finishing second.

Football is not a school exam where you disqualify the winner and automatically give the prize to the runner-up. Spurs finished seven points behind Chelsea.

You would have to establish not only that Chelsea broke rules but that the breach justified removing the title and that Spurs should inherit it. That is a high bar.

What Pochettino is absolutely right about, though, is that punishment has to mean something.

A fine, however large, can look rather different to a football club than a sporting sanction.



And that brings us back to City. If the allegations are ultimately proven, the question is not simply: How much should they pay?

It will be: What sporting consequence, if any, properly reflects what happened? That is why this case matters so much.

I am not suggesting for a second that an independent commission should rush a decision simply because football is impatient. But patience has a funny quality when you are the person paying for it — and the other clubs have been paying.



They have already spent tens of millions. If City win, the other clubs will have to pick up their legal bill, estimated to be around £100million. Then comes another extraordinary detail. When the decision is reached, the Prem board and City will know the verdict three days before it is made public.

City know. The Prem board knows. Everyone else waits.

And still, officially, the answer is: “I can’t comment.”

Perhaps that is right. But when people are denied information, they start guessing.

That is why I suspect the other clubs are less interested in some grand conspiracy than they are in something much more mundane.



They want to know what is taking so long. They want to know what they are paying for and when it will end.

If City are cleared, football needs to accept it. If found guilty, football needs to accept that too, and deal with the consequences.

But after all these years, all the charges and tens of millions spent in legal costs, the Prem is entitled to expect its independent process to reach the finishing line.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Not because City deserve to lose or because the other clubs deserve to win. Simply because eventually, even in football, there has to be an answer.

Right now, there isn’t.

Sports.title: Former Sky Sports reporter and Ronnie O’Sullivan’s ex reveals why she’ll NEVER work in football again
Sports.content:
FORMER Sky Sports reporter Bianca Westwood has claimed she will “probably” never work in football again.

The 51-year-old took a voluntary redundancy from Sky in 2023 after 22 years with the broadcaster.



Westwood became popular with fans after making a name for herself as a pitchside reporter during their hit Soccer Saturday show.

But now she has started a new career venture posting about fashion and beauty on social media.



And Westwood – who dated Snooker legend Ronnie O’Sullivan in the early 2000s – explained why she is leaning towards a future as an influencer rather than returning to football.

She said in a TiKTok video: “I wanted to set a few things straight because I still get a lot of messages asking about Sky.



“When am I going back to Sky? When am I doing the football again? The compliments are really nice, I do appreciate them, but I’m not going back to Sky.

“The thing is, I’m not going back to Sky and I’m probably never going to work in football again.

“I had a feeling, probably about a year before I left Sky that the opportunities were becoming few and far between, they didn’t really rate me, that’s why I started doing the fashion, beauty and skincare, things that I love as a woman.

“All my content now is geared towards women so I don’t even know why I get new male followers because the football has gone.

“Three years ago, Sky offered me redundancy, I decided to take it. Jeff [Stelling] was leaving at the same time, I thought it was probably the best time to go and that was basically the reasons behind my decision so I’m not really going to go back.”

United take on their neighbours after winning just one of their first three league matches, meaning even victory won't be enough to lift them above City. "Results-wise, it hasn't been the start we wanted, we wanted more points in the league," Carrick admitted after the Sabah victory.

‌



There has been excitement this season about the return of Marcus Rashford and the progress of JJ Gabriel, though there's a chance neither will start on Sunday. We've got updates on both players as we bring you the latest lines from around Old Trafford.

Lisando Martinez trolls Jamie Carragher as Man Utd star leaves Micah Richards in hysterics READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher warns Michael Carrick he faces same problem as Gareth Southgate READ MORE :

Barca chief explains Rashford snub

Marcus Rashford hit double-figures for goals and assists at Barcelona last summer and yet the club opted against turning his loan into a permanent move. The Catalan club instead moved for Rashford's England team-mate Anthony Gordon and their sporting director Deco explained why they felt Gordon was the better fit.

‌



"One of the things we saw that was difficult last year was the fact that, when we were without Raphinha, the team's energy seemed to drop," Deco told Marca. "We looked at many wingers, but signing players in the Premier League is almost impossible, you see the figures involved.

"He (Gordon_ was the profile that best fit. The great advantage is that the players are excited to come to our project."

United coach lays out Gabriel's path

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel starred for United against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League (Image: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock)

‌



JJ Gabriel got a taste of first-team action in pre-season, but the United prodigy is still waiting for his competitive debut. However, academy coach Adam Lawrence shed some light on the teenager's path forward after an eye-catching hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League.

"JJ is surrounded by people that really believe in him," Lawrence said. "From the top of the club right the way through. Where he's been at the club for so long, he's got good relationships with the players, with the staff.

"Over the course of time that helps as well. At the moment just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, making sure that he's getting the right exposure across different levels.

Article continues below

"We're obviously not perfect but it's definitely something we put a lot of thought into. So yeah, it's good to see him just enjoying his football and in a good place for sure."

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer admission made after dramatic £47m deal collapse
Sports.content:
Chelsea transfer admission made after dramatic £47m deal collapse

Chelsea had a £47million transfer dramatically collapse late on deadline day after waiting weeks this summer before they sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City

View 2 Images Monaco denied Lamine Camara a transfer to Chelsea on deadline day (Image: Franco Arland, Getty Images)

Lamine Camara has admitted that another opportunity to leave Monaco could arise after they reneged on an agreement with Chelsea during transfer deadline day. They had a £47million deal in place before the Ligue 1 club made a last-minute U-turn to keep their player while negotiating Folarin Balogun's prospective £42.5million move to Everton.

‌



Camara, 22, was the subject of two offers before Monaco reduced their asking price. They did so after concerns surfaced during the United States international's medical tests.

‌



However, neither player left the principality for England; both stayed put. Camara has now spoken about the situation 10 days later.

‌



Behdad Eghbali's net worth compared to Premier League rivals ahead of full Chelsea takeover READ MORE :

Todd Boehly era at Chelsea nearly over with talks accelerating for duo to sell shares READ MORE :

During a Monaco press conference on Friday, the Senegal international said: "It was a somewhat turbulent and difficult time. But that's part of a player's life.

"I tried to remain professional, avoid dwelling on it, and move on so I could quickly focus on the upcoming match in Paris (three days later). Once it was over, there was no point in thinking about it.

"Did I want to go to Chelsea? Saying that now would imply I'm no longer fully present with the team. Yes, there was a possibility I might leave, but it didn't happen at the last minute.

‌



View 2 Images Lamine Camara will continue to play for Monaco until at least January (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

"These things happen; look at the example of Julian Alvarez with Atletico Madrid. It happens all over the world, and I'm trying to turn the page as quickly as possible to focus on the season."

Speaking about the possibility of interest from other clubs down the line, Camara said: "If it doesn't come back around, it will be because I gave up or didn't work hard enough. If I keep going like this, I know I can help the team perform well.

‌



"Football moves fast, and perhaps other chances will arise. But for now, I'm staying focused on the season."

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro defended their approach hours after the window shut. The club's sporting director said: "There is no deal on Lamine because it's also fair to do this. It's also part of the game.

Article continues below

"There's no reason that this kind of discussion or dynamic on the last day of the transfer window, which all of us decided to be on the last day, trying to find solutions with the clock ticking in our neck, that now this kind of interaction becomes the bad guys in the room, that Monaco is not fair, Monaco is not right.

"Everybody is very fair and nice in the football industry, just Monaco is not too much, so this is the storytelling."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sends warning to Arsenal's Premier League title rivals as secret target set
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sends warning to Arsenal's Premier League title rivals as secret target set

Arsenal have enjoyed a brilliant start to their title defence with the Gunners catching the eye with some of their recent performances under Mikel Arteta this term

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta takes his Arsenal side to Sunderland this weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta is enjoying Arsenal being the great entertainers - but insists they can get even better. The reigning champions have started the season in real style with three straight wins in the Premier League and they have played free-flowing football.

‌



Arsenal were christened Set Piece FC last season because they were so good at scoring from corners and free kicks but all of their goals this term have been from open play.

‌



Arteta says that is down to having the likes of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz back to form and full fitness but he has set a target to play with more “flair” this season.

‌



They face Sunderland on Saturday night on the back of an impressive Champions League win at Napoli when they dominated but only had Odegaard’s goal to show for their dominance.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Gunners boss Arteta says he wants his players to be more efficient and ruthless with their finishing as they look to defend their title. Arteta, whose side travel to Sunderland on Saturday night, said: “I like a lot what I’ve seen from the team so far.

“For sure, it’s for flair but also just making sure what happens on the pitch is what we want. And having that dominance and control and threat in our minds.

“It’s the way we have to continue and evolve in certain areas and that is an area that we have put a lot of emphasis into and now we have a lot of players back.

‌



“The opportunities and synergies that we create with the team are much stronger and we’re going to continue to be like that. That’s always the intention.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is aiming to claim back-to-back Premier League titles this season (Image: Getty Images)

“Sometimes it’s the level of the opponents, sometimes the level of execution and that has to increase as well to be much more efficient and dominant throughout the games and we will continue to do that.”

‌



Arteta has been fulsome in his praise for captain Odegaard who looks back to form, fitness and sharpness after an injury-plagued couple of seasons.

Odegaard scored the winner at Chelsea last Sunday, again at Napoli in the Champions League in midweek and Arteta also says Havertz’s return has also been key.

Arteta says Havertz’s intelligence means he is ahead of everyone else on the pitch and therefore it is difficult to pin down his best position.

‌



View 3 Images Kai Havertz has had a bright start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Arteta said: “The best position is in relation to what the game demands and what the team demands on the day. To be as efficient as possible, as unpredictable as possible. Kai is extremely intelligent, that's his biggest quality.

“He understands the game, he's five, ten seconds ahead of the game, he knows what he's having, he doesn't need to think about it, he just acts. And he just makes the people around him better, which is another massive quality.

‌



“On top of that, he's scoring goals, he's producing chances, his work rate, as we all know, is just outstanding. And he's in a great emotional state at the moment.”

Arteta also praised the impact of one of the club’s new summer signings as Ezri Konsa - who joined in a £55m deal from Aston Villa - has looked at home immediately.

Arsenal were held to a 2-2 draw at Sunderland last season and their back four is certain to be tested again with Arteta insisting Konsa’s personality and defensive abilities have been key.

‌



Arteta added: “Well, it's certainly something to admire because it's not easy at all and you should not take it for granted. But after talking to a lot of people that have worked with him, whether staff members or players, I already had a sense the way everybody was talking about him.

“That he's a person that is great at gathering people together. He has a real personality, a lot of leadership skills.

“And you saw the first day, he just trained the way he was talking, the way he was presenting himself. It was very impressive and so far he's done a really good job.”

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim reignites feud with Man Utd legends after failed tenure - 'they talk a lot'
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim reignites feud with Man Utd legends after failed tenure - 'they talk a lot'

Ruben Amorim had to deal with constant opinions during his Manchester United tenure as former players cast their views and the now AC Milan boss has fired a dig at them

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim has taken a swipe at Man Utd's former players

Former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim has taken charge at the club's former players who now work in the media, claiming they "talk a lot about things" from a different era.

‌



The Portuguese coach is now in charge of AC Milan, landing the job at San Siro just months after he was dismissed by the Old Trafford hierarchy. Amorim presided over United's worst-ever Premier League finish and won just 24 of his 63 games.

‌



Milan, like United, has a huge history and has ruled Europe in the past with a number of its former greats giving their opinions on the current state of affairs. That was something Amorim regularly had to deal with when he was at the helm in Manchester.

‌



Gary Neville is one of the country's most high profile pundits whilst the likes of Roy Keane, Nicky Butt and Paul Scholes all hold positions within the media and give their take on current affairs, which saw Amorim under the spotlight.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



When pressed on how it feels to have club legends commenting Amorim replied: "I was in a club [Manchester United] in the past with a lot of legends, and they have big opinions, and they talk a lot about things. They lived in a time that was completely different."

The bulk of the United-associated pundits played during their trophy-laden era when Sir Alex Ferguson was in charge. The Red Devils were the dominant force in the Premier League and serially qualified for the Champions League.

Nowadays United are a shadow of the side they once were. Their wait for a league title has extended to 13 years and they're by no means regulars at Europe's top table.

‌



View 2 Images Ruben Amorim struggled throughout his Man Utd tenure (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Scholes once claimed that Amorim was not "the right man" and doesn't "get the club" before his United exit - with the Milan coach saying at the time that the former players "didn't have all the information" when they made their comments.

"I think it's normal," he said. "I think it's a fact that me, as a manager of Manchester United, I think we are underachieving. We should have more points, especially this season. So I take that naturally.

Article continues below

"Sometimes they don't have all the information and they see Manchester United with the standards that they lived here, always winning. So it's hard for them to see their club in this situation."

Sports.title: Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, 34, charged with assaulting wife as ex-Premier League star set for trial
Sports.content:
Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, 34, charged with assaulting wife as ex-Premier League star set for trial

Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, who played for Cardiff City in the Premier League, attended Magistrates Court where he learned his trial date

View 3 Images Nathaniel Mendez-Laing now plays for MK Dons (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

MK Dons player Nathaniel Mendez-Laing has appeared in court, where he has denied claims he assaulted his wife.

‌



The former Premier League ace stands accused of attacking his wife, Saira Mendez-Laing, while they were in their home in Shenstone, Staffordshire. The incident was alleged to have taken place in June.

‌



He was arrested and charged with assault by beating after the police were called to their house. In magistrates' court on Friday September 11, he denied one count of assault by beating.

‌



Mendez-Laing was on crutches as he arrived wearing a black suit with white shirt. During his appearance at Cannock magistrates' court, he only confirmed his name, age and address.

In August, it's understood the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) authorised charges.

View 3 Images Nathaniel Mendez-Laing appeared in magistrates' court (Image: Instagram)

‌



The MK Dons ace was freed on conditional bail by the court. This was granted by District Judge Joseph O'Connor, who also stated the player will stand trial next January.

Mendez-Laing made 20 Premier League appearances for Cardiff City, where he contributed four goals and one assist.

He now plays for the Dons in League One, having moved to the club from Derby County last summer. While he was born in Birmingham, he is a Guatemala international.

‌



He qualifies for the Central American country, who he has amassed 20 caps with, as both his mother and grand mother hail from the Latin American nation.

View 3 Images Mendez-Laing played in the Premier League with Cardiff City (Image: 2018 AMA Sports Photo Agency)

The player chose to represent Guatemala having previously made appeared for the England U17s when he was a youngster.

Article continues below

Throughout his career, the wide midfielder has also represented Wolverhampton Wanderers, Peterborough, Sheffield United, Portsmouth, Shrewsbury, Cambridge United, Rochdale, Middlesbrough and Sheffield Wednesday.

Mendez-Lain and Saira married in June last year. After they tied the knot, the Dons uploaded a congratulatory post on the club's social media accounts.

His club have said they will not comment on ongoing legal proceedings.

Sports.title: Michail Antonio returns to English football nearly two years after brutal car crash
Sports.content:
Michail Antonio returns to English football nearly two years after brutal car crash

Michail Antonio spent a period with Qatari side Al-Sailiya following his exit from West Ham after his devastating car crash but the Jamaican forward has now made a return to English football

View 2 Images Michail Antonio has finally found his next club (Image: Getty Images)

Michail Antonio has penned a one-year deal with Watford to make his return to English football. The former West Ham star has been without a club since leaving Qatari side Al-Sailiya in the summer.

‌



Antonio, now 36, had been in the Middle East for a brief spell having been a free agent following a devastating car crash in December 2024.

‌



Speaking after his move was made official, Antonio said: “It’s a good set of boys here. They are focused and ready to show their abilities this season.

‌



“Watford is a big club and hopefully I can come in and bring success and help wherever I can. I’ve scored a few goals against Watford! So hopefully I can score some for Watford now when I’m fully up to speed."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Antonio could make his debut for his new club this weekend as Watford come up against Stoke City at Vicarage Road. The Hornets currently sit 12th in the Championship after six games.

Antonio’s move signals his first return to English football following his exit from West Ham. Prior to that, he was involved in a car crash in December 2024, and was close to losing his life.

Speaking to the BBC about the crash, Antonio said: "It's weird, because the whole way through this, I have been told that I was awake and was speaking to everybody - the police, the people, and the person who found me.

‌



"My leg was completely shattered and they got me out and put a splint on it by the side of the car. Everyone believed I got an air ambulance out, but the helicopter couldn't get off the ground because of the storm, so I was driven to the hospital."

View 2 Images Michail Antonio has not made an appearance in English football since leaving West Ham (Image: Getty Images)

On seeing the wreckage of his car, he added: "It gave me a weird feeling in my stomach. It just made me realise how close I was to dying. I had seen the pictures but it was 10 times worse in person. The car was an absolute mess. It was difficult for me."

Article continues below

Antonio has represented Reading, Cheltenham Town, Southampton, Colchester United, Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest throughout his career. He joined West Ham in 2015 and went on to score 83 goals in 323 appearances for the Hammers, while he helped the side to the Conference League title in 2023.

Antonio was previously close to moves to both Leicester City and Brentford over the past year but neither side agreed a deal with the Jamaican international.

Sports.title: Man Utd confirm 685 season ticket bans as touting investigation sparks furious backlash
Sports.content:
Man Utd confirm 685 season ticket bans as touting investigation sparks furious backlash

Manchester United have announced the results of their controversial investigation into ticket touting at Old Trafford, which has sparked a planned protest this weekend

View 3 Images Manchester United fans have criticised the club's investigation (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

Manchester United have removed 685 season tickets following a lengthy and much-criticised investigation into touting at Old Trafford.

‌



Back in August, the club identified 1,617 accounts exhibiting "unusual activity". The holders of those accounts were then contacted and asked to provide explanations for the activity that was deemed suspicious.

‌



This heavy-handed approach sparked a furious backlash among supporters, with many believing that innocent and loyal fans were unfairly being accused. A protest ahead of Sunday's Manchester Derby at Old Trafford has been called over what fan group The 1958 said were sanctions being made without "compelling evidence".

‌



United have now announced the results of their investigation, which allowed fans to appeal to an independent appeals panel. The club said 685 season tickets were revoked, including 499 whereby a ban was upheld by the appeals panel.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Meanwhile, 468 cases were resolved after the season ticket holder provided information to exonerate themselves. The club have admitted they "did not anticipate the extent" to which fans shared account details "in circumstances they regarded as legitimate" and in those cases no sanctions were imposed.

The club said in a statement: "Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts.

"These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United.

‌



"Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list."

View 3 Images Manchester United fans are unhappy with the way the touting investigation was carried out (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

The club added: "We want to allow any sanctioned ticket holder the opportunity to refer their case to the Independent Football Ombudsman. Therefore, we will wait until after the international break before reallocating season tickets.

‌



"Any seats used on a match-by-match basis before then will be sold at season ticket prices, not matchday prices. The club is not profiting from this process."

The club said 226 accounts received final warnings for breaking rules but not for financial gain, while 238 accounts guilty of further abuses saw their initial season ticket ban reduced to a ban on home ticket forwarding and away match applications.

Speaking before the club's announcement on Friday, Chris Rumfitt, a spokesperson for Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST), summed up the ill feeling among fans.

‌



He told Mirror Football: "If it was a clampdown on touting we would be entirely supportive, because the biggest losers of touting are fans who get exploited and ripped off.

View 3 Images Ticket prices have been another bone of contention (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

"But what they are calling a clampdown on touting has brought up a huge numbers of match-going fans doing ordinary things match-going fans do, i.e. passing tickets between groups of friends at face value, which people wouldn't consider to be touting.

‌



"There is no question that large number of ordinary fans have been caught up in this because what the club has defined as 'suspicious' included lots of things fans do."

Rumfitt believes the issue has touched such a nerve with supporters that only the botched attempt to form a European Super League five years ago compares to the strength of feeling in the stands.

He added: "The approach the club has taken has been 'ban first, ask questions later'. They've banned people and then asked them to prove that they haven't done anything wrong, which isn't normally how things work in this country. The burden of proof works the other way around.

Article continues below

"There's a massive amount of discontent among all fan groups, it's really united the fans. The way the club has gone about this is completely wrong. It has spread further mistrust."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick makes Bruno Fernandes promise as Man Utd star spotted limping
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick makes Bruno Fernandes promise as Man Utd star spotted limping

Manchester United are set to take on local rivals Manchester City on Sunday afternoon just days after their Champions League victory against Sabah at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Fernandes has had a hectic start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has promised Bruno Fernandes a rest after he played the full 90 minutes against Sabah. The Portuguese playmaker has had a hectic start to the season, having played four successive full games.

‌



In that time, he has scored four goals including one in United’s Champions League opener against Sabah. United boss Carrick opted for widespread changes in the second-half, albeit Fernandes stayed on.

‌



And that appeared to have cost the Red Devils, with the 32-year-old having been spotted limping away from Old Trafford. Asked about his changes, Carrick said he ran out of changes but has promised Fernandes that he will get the chance for a rest soon.

‌



"We only had five subs! We had to make certain decisions on what that looked like," said Carrick. "But, of course, he's like anybody else. He has played an awful lot, but I think we're developing the group and the squad to be able to accommodate that in different ways.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"Tonight was just one of those things, there were decisions to be made and he ended up staying on."

Another concern that United have ahead of the Manchester derby is the fitness of Luke Shaw, who was left out of the side against Sabah.

Asked about the defender, Carrick added: "We'll have to see. We just kind of looked after him a little bit going into tonight. He wasn't quite ready for it 100%, so we didn't risk it. We'll see how he is over the next couple of days or so."

‌



Alongside Shaw, Marcus Rashford was also a notable absence against Sabah, but Carrick has assured that he is not dealing with an injury.

View 2 Images Fernandes was seen limping after the win against Sabah (Image: Getty Images)

Asked if it was more of a precaution, the United boss added: "A little bit of that, yeah, and trying to share the load a little bit, to a point, as well.

‌



"We've got good options, so we're trying to keep everyone fresh, but with a point where Ben [Šeško] can get good minutes tonight [against Sabah] and get him up to speed.

"There's always a bit of a challenge in getting that right, but it was nice to keep Marcus fresh and ready for the weekend.”

United certainly face a tough task this weekend as they welcome a Man City side to Old Trafford who have enjoyed a perfect start to the season. Enzo Maresca’s side sit top of the early table after three wins, while they also saw off Portuguese giants Porto in their Champions League opener in midweek.
