World.title: Mexico rescues eight from clandestine clinic run by violent Jalisco cartel
World.content:
Mexican law enforcement has said it rescued eight people who had been forcibly recruited by the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), one of the country’s most powerful and violent drug trafficking organisations.

The eight people were found at a clandestine clinic on a farm in the municipality of Tecalitlan, in the western state of Jalisco, roughly 160 kilometres (100 miles) from Guadalajara, the AFP news agency reported.

Images released by state prosecutors showed dimly lit rooms with mattresses on the floor and heavily stained walls. One photo showed a cap bearing an image of Jesus Malverde, a folk figure widely revered by drug traffickers as an unofficial patron saint.

Jalisco state prosecutor Salvador Gonzalez said the property “operated as a place to shelter people recruited by organised crime who, for one reason or another, ended up injured in connection with the activities they were made to carry out and needed to recover”.

He added the victims “had been deprived of their freedom”. Two of those rescued were on crutches. Authorities said they also seized illegal drugs and narcotics, as well as weapons and ammunition. Six suspected guards, aged 21 to 48, were also arrested.

Investigators found the site while searching for a 20-year-old man who had gone missing in late July after leaving his home in Tlaquepaque, near Guadalajara, in a taxi to answer what he believed was a job offer at a farm.

The case echoes the 2025 discovery of a suspected CJNG training camp at a ranch in Teuchitlan, also in Jalisco, where a civilian search collective found clothing, luggage and human remains, leading to more than 40 arrests.



An estimated 134,000 people are believed to be missing across Mexico, with Jalisco having one of the country’s highest rates of missing people.

Mexico’s government said last week it had disabled more than 1,700 social media profiles spreading fake job offers to lure young people into crime.

World.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles off eastern coast, Seoul says
World.content:
South Korea said it boosted its surveillance posture and was closely exchanging information on the launches with the US and Japan.

North Korea has fired ballistic missiles towards the sea off its eastern coast, according to South Korea’s military.

South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said that it detected several missiles launched from North Korea’s eastern coastal area of Wonsan about 5:20am on Saturday (20:20 GMT on Friday), which flew about 250 kilometres (155 miles). It added that it is closely exchanging information on the launches with the United States and Japan.

South Korea’s presidential National Security Office said it held an emergency security meeting with the Defence Ministry, the JCS and other relevant agencies following the launch.

The US Pacific Command said North Korea’s launch event does not pose an immediate threat to US territory or to its allies, adding that Washington remains committed to the defence of South Korea and its other allies in the region.

The missiles were launched a day after South Korea concluded five days of joint maritime drills with the US and Japan that were focused on North Korea.

Hours after the exercises began on Monday, North Korea’s defence minister, Kim Song Gi, criticised the exercise and warned North Korea was capable of taking “strong and reflective countermeasures from the standpoint of power”.

Late last month, North Korea slammed plans for the so-called Freedom Edge exercises in international waters off South Korea as a “threat” to Pyongyang and other countries in the region.

The North also fired a barrage of missiles into the sea on August 20, despite an overture from US President Donald Trump, who said he planned to meet this year with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.



The August launch from the nuclear-armed North came as South Korea and the US held a shorter edition of their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercises, following an order from Trump to scale back the drills.

The order from Trump, who called the exercises “inappropriate and hostile” towards North Korea, alarmed US allies in the region.

Pyongyang has long condemned US-South Korea joint exercises as rehearsals for invasion, often staging missile launches around the drills.

World.title: Putin and Pezeshkian call out US dominance ahead of BRICS
World.content:
NewsFeed Putin and Pezeshkian call out US dominance ahead of BRICS

The presidents of Iran and Russia have criticised US dollar dominance ahead of the BRICS summit in India. Countering the US role in the global economy, and the effects of its war on Iran, are expected to lead the agenda as the 11-nation bloc meets on September 12.

World.title: Satellite image shows critical Saudi pipeline damaged in drone attack
World.content:
NewsFeed Satellite image shows critical Saudi pipeline damaged in drone attack

Saudi Arabia has shut its East-West oil pipeline after a drone attack. Riyadh says the attack originated in Iraq. The pipeline allowed Riyadh to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: CIA releases dozens of declassified documents on bin Laden prior to 9/11
World.content:
A briefer wrote to then-President Clinton that bin Laden’s ‘preferred option is to strike the US on its own soil in Washington’, and that al-Qaeda ‘may fly an explosive-packed airplane into a US city’.

Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, attacks detail intelligence government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaeda leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended the United States’ national security.

The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the US and other countries, including how his operations were financed.

Proclaiming it “an act of exceptional transparency”, CIA Director John Ratcliffe said the documents were the agency’s single largest release of declassified presidential daily briefs — the highly classified briefings prepared by the nation’s intelligence community for the government’s most senior leaders.

The documents range from a February 1998 file, prepared for then-President Bill Clinton, titled “Terrorists Seeking WMD Capability” and mentioning bin Laden and other Islamic extremists, to a September 12, 2001, report in which a source indicated the attacks had been planned for two years and had also targeted the US Capitol.

An April 1998 document described the Taliban’s unwillingness to hand over bin Laden, at the time seen as their “guest” in Afghanistan, noting their “gratitude for his assistance during the Soviet occupation” was making them “reluctant to alienate him by monitoring or controlling his activities”.



Five months later, a briefer wrote that bin Laden’s “preferred option is to strike the US on its own soil in Washington” and that al-Qaeda “may fly an explosive-packed airplane into a US city”.

Potential hijackings were also discussed in December 1998, when a briefer described how conspirators “have evaded security checks during a recent trial run at an unidentified New York airport”, and “some members of the Bin Ladin network have received hijack training”.

Other documents detail bin Laden’s pursuit of materials for making “dirty bombs”, conventional weapons infused with radioactive material. By June 1999, according to intelligence officials, his operatives had conducted such experiments with explosives to “increase their energy output”.

Many of the documents were redacted to conceal sources’ names and other identifying information. They didn’t appear to break any new ground on the planning of the attacks or on US officials’ understanding of how they had unfolded.

World.title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
World.content:
Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was attacked by drones launched from Iraq, as conflict in the Middle East widens.

Iraq said it had fired a military commander and launched an investigation after admitting the drone attack on its neighbour's East-West pipeline had originated in one of its provinces bordering Iran.

The 1,200km (745 mile) pipeline has helped Saudi Arabia - the world's largest crude oil exporter - bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The incident comes amid a major advance by the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, putting more pressure on global oil shipping routes as the US-Iran war stretches into its seventh month.

Riyadh on Friday said it had shut the pipeline as a precaution, as satellite images of scorched ground and smoke near the site emerged.

The foreign ministry said the attack resulted in some injuries and damage, which was still being assessed.

The pipeline has been moving 4% to 5% of global oil supply, news agency Reuters has reported, citing ship tracking companies and analysts.

Saudi Arabia has chosen not to retaliate at this stage, its foreign ministry says, following a call from Iraq's prime minister.

It said the kingdom would "support the efforts of the Iraqi government" to "prevent attacks" launched from the country against neighbouring states.

"The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia affirms that it reserves its right to take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty and security, protect its facilities, and ensure the safety of its citizens and residents," the statement added.

The Iraqi prime minister's office in its own statement said the operations commander in the Maysan governorate - a province which borders Iran - had been removed from his post following confirmation the drone attack had been launched from that region.

World.title: Tragic death of woman who testified against father in notorious mafia murder of mother
World.content:
A woman who testified against her own father after her mother was murdered in a notorious mafia killing in Italy is believed to have taken her own life.

Denise Cosco was found critically injured on Sunday and died later in hospital in Rome.

Her mother Lea Garofalo, who was killed in 2009, became a powerful symbol of resistance to the mafia after turning witness for the state against the 'Ndrangheta clan in southern Italy.

Those close to Cosco recall her bravery in speaking out at her father's trial, but also her tremendous struggle in the years that followed.

At 35, she died at the same age her mother was when she was murdered.

Enza Rando, a senator and anti-mafia lawyer who represented Cosco at the murder trial, described her death as "a profound wound for the entire country", and proof that the mafia not only kills, but creates "true monsters in the lives and souls" of those who survive.

Francesca Rispoli, co-president of the anti-mafia organisation Libera, said the death highlighted the struggle experienced by many who break with organised crime.

"The mafia, it's not just something physical. You can leave. You can change your name," she told the BBC. "But there is still a tie, a family tie, that staysâ¦ deep inside and is impossible to overcome."

Cosco, like her mother, had lived under state protection with a new name and identity for many years.

But Rispoli said she remained extremely vulnerable and had reconnected with her father, Carlo Cosco, in prison in recent years because, despite everything, she had felt a "hole in her life".

Friends say she struggled with mental health problems and addiction.

"Maybe this is a sign that those trying to lead another life need more support. Not just for one year â maybe their whole life," Rispoli argued, as organised crime groups in Italy â especially the 'Ndrangheta - involve close-knit family networks.

In Cosco's case, both her mother's family and her father were tied to the mafia.

She had always refused to believe her father's story that her mother had abandoned her to start a new life in Australia.

In fact, he had tricked Garofalo to a meeting, then had her strangled, her body dismembered then incinerated.

Several years later, a statement by one of the killers finally allowed police to recover some fragments of bone and a necklace, which Cosco identified.

At a public funeral in 2013, she spoke of her mother's courage in "putting herself on the lineâ¦ for justice for all".

Her father and three accomplices were already serving life in prison.

At the trial, Cosco described herself as a "proud witness for justice" and said she had taken the difficult choice to testify â speaking from behind a screen â because she wanted "inner freedom to start over" with her life.

Prosecutors have now opened an investigation to determine whether there was any incitement to suicide and her phone has been seized for analysis.

Friends and supporters were due to gather in Milan on Friday evening to remember her near the spot where her mother was abducted.

"Denise's entire life revolved between the two extremes of courage and suffering," Luigi Ciotti, president of Libera wrote, calling that a difficult balance.

"Today, something in that fragile equilibrium was broken forever."

If you or someone you know are affected by the issues raised in this story, the BBC Action Line has information on organisations that can offer advice and support.

World.title: Death toll from Philippines ferry fire climbs to 35, with dozens still missing
World.content:
The Philippine Coast Guard says it has recovered 30 bodies from the wreckage of a ferry that caught fire this week, bringing the total death toll to 35.

More than 130 people were on board the MV June Aster when the blaze erupted on Wednesday as it neared its destination at the tourist hotspot of Coron, after departing from Manila.

Forty-three people were rescued, with many receiving treatment in hospital, and searches continue for more than 50 people who remain unaccounted for.

The country's coast guard says more bodies remain on the boat, which they were unable to board until Friday due to toxic fumes and lingering heat.

In a press conference, coast guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said most bodies had been retrieved from the sleeping area of the boat, which had been making a 22-hour journey.

"Agencies are currently undertaking the proper recovery and identification of the remains in accordance with established procedures," Cayabyab said.

"We recognise the grief of the families affected by this tragic incident."

Earlier, the coast guard said preliminary interviews with the survivors suggest that the fire started in the cargo hold. Some passengers were not wearing life vests, they noted.

A survivor who was hauled to safety on a rescue boat told the BBC he had heard frantic cries onboard when the fire erupted, and was trampled by panicked people as he tried to escape.

The Philippines' maritime authority is investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The ferry, built in 2002, held valid safety certificates and passed an enforcement inspection in March, but investigators are looking into potential manifest discrepancies, cargo loading integrity, and crew emergency response protocols, the Palawan Daily reported.

The vessel was carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members.

Atienza Interisland Ferries, the vessel's operator, has pledged full cooperation with the inquiry.

"Our hearts remain with the affected families, and we will not rest until all individuals are accounted for," the company said in a statement on Thursday.

World.title: Passenger train derails in France leaving at least 44 injured
World.content:
At least 44 people have been injured, including one seriously, after a passenger train derailed in northern France, local officials have said.

An 18-year-old woman was airlifted in critical condition by helicopter to hospital.

Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said 180 passengers were on board the train that was operating between Rouen and Caen in Normandy.

He added that 140 firefighters and other emergency teams were being deployed to the scene of the crash on Friday evening near the commune of ClÃ©on, just south of Rouen.

The cause of the derailment was not immediately known.

The local authorities activated a mass-casualty response plan after the crash shortly before 20:00 local time (18:00 GMT).

Photographs later emerged showing passengers leaving the crashed train, with French media reporting that three carriages overturned.

France's state-owned railway operator SNCF reported "significant disruptions" on its routes in the area. It said replacement buses would be provided.

The authorities advised the public to avoid the area.

World.title: Arrest made over the death of black woman found hanged from tree in Mississippi
World.content:
Warning: This story contains distressing details

Police in the US state of Mississippi have arrested a man in connection with the death of a black woman found hanged from a tree, and say they could soon take more people into custody.

Tasia Fortune's body was found in the lot of an abandoned home in Jackson in August, but police only announced they were treating her death as a possible homicide earlier this week.

"That arrest today is an important development in this investigation, but it is not the conclusion," Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney said on Friday. "This case remains active."

Fortune's death has worried locals in Jackson, a majority-black city in a state with a history of racial violence and lynching.

During Friday's news conference, Brackney said the medical examiner had confirmed Fortune's cause of death was homicide and said there would be a murder charge.

She identified the suspect as Jarques Ratliff, 51, and said there was an "association" between Ratliff, who is also black, and Fortune, but would not elaborate further.

"Additional arrests will be pending as our investigators continue to follow the evidence," Brackney said, adding that they had interviewed 15 people in the case.

Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, told the BBC that she cried when police called to update her about the arrest, saying: "I guess I do feel like a little sigh of relief...like a little bit of peace just come over me."

"I just hope that they've got the right person," she added.

The arrest of a suspect followed weeks of what Spivey and residents in Jackson described as relative silence and inaction from local officials.

Combined with the grim nature of Fortune's death and Mississippi's history of racial lynchings, the lack of information about the case had left the community in shock and fear.

Spivey earlier told the BBC she had tried contacting Jackson police several times over the last two weeks, leaving multiple voicemails, and had not heard back.

Brackney addressed the family's frustration on Friday, saying: "We have been in constant contact with the mother and the stepfather, as well as the biological father, throughout this case."

A letter Spivey wrote to officials about the limited communication and speed of the investigation was read during a public city meeting on Tuesday - moments before Jackson police made the announcement about a possible homicide.

"I'm kind of like in awe," Spivey said. "Like, I can't believe it. That was quick."

Earlier this month, Fortune's death was described by a member of the US Congress as part of a pattern of "possible modern-day lynchings".

More than 50 members of Congress this week sent a letter, external to the FBI and justice department, saying they were "extremely alarmed by reports of black people found hanging from trees in numerous states" and calling for an independent investigation into the deaths of black Americans.

"The series of deaths raise significant suspicion of foul play given the role of lynching in our nation's history," it states.

So far this year there have been at least 10 reported hangings of black people in the US, they said, adding that there were more than 70 lynchings documented between 2000 and 2025.

World.title: Israel says it has destroyed major underground Hezbollah base
World.content:
Israel's military says it has destroyed a large underground complex operated by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

It said it used more than 1,000 tonnes of explosives to destroy two tunnels spanning more than 2km (1.2 miles) beneath the Ali Taher Ridge.

The blast triggered seismic activity equivalent to a magnitude 4.1 earthquake, according to the US Geological Survey.

There was no immediate public response from Hezbollah or the Lebanese government.

Israeli forces took control of the ridge last week after months of fighting with the Iran-backed group there. The Israeli military occupies a large swathe of southern Lebanon captured after the conflict with Hezbollah resumed in March.

Images released by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) showed a fireball lighting up the sky.

"The sky lit up and about 15 seconds later we heard the terrifying sound," Ahamed, a resident in Nabatieh, about 6km west of the ridge, told the BBC.

"The house shook all together as if it was literally an earthquake."

He said people were screaming and children were crying, and that cars filled the roads as people left the area for Beirut.

Tremors were even felt in the coastal city of Saida 40km north.

The IDF said the underground infrastructure included a command centre used by Hezbollah's Badr unit and contained dozens of rockets, missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles, as well as anti-tank weapons, mines and explosives.

"This was strategic infrastructure that was constructed over two decades, funded and planned by the Iranian terror regime," the IDF said in a statement on Telegram.

"All of the terrorists who were inside the infrastructure were eliminated or fled."

The IDF said the destruction of the complex completed a mission to destroy eight tunnels and establish a "security zone" in the area.

The latest action comes amid renewed fighting in southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces have expanded operations against Hezbollah positions and continue to hold what Israel describes as a security zone near the border.

Lebanese media reported fresh Israeli strikes elsewhere in the south on Thursday, including Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Mansouri in the Tyre district.

The Lebanese army has increased deployments in areas outside Israeli control, including the southern city of Nabatieh, in efforts to strengthen stability and reassure residents, local television station MTV reported.

Lebanon was drawn into the war between Israel, the US and Iran on 2 March, when Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for a strike that killed Iran's supreme leader.

Israel responded by launching a bombing campaign across Lebanon and invading a significant part of the country's south. Its forces continue to occupy roughly 5% of Lebanese territory.

Fighting decreased following a ceasefire deal between Iran and the US in June, alongside a separate agreement between Lebanon and Israel.

The UN says about 330,000 people in Lebanon remain displaced by the conflict, with Israeli military activity, air strikes, destruction and restrictions on returning to Israeli-occupied areas preventing many from going home.

Under the Lebanon-Israel framework, Hezbollah is expected to disarm, Israeli forces to withdraw gradually from southern Lebanon and the Lebanese army to deploy across the area.

Hezbollah was not directly involved in the agreement and has rejected direct negotiations.

Despite a reduction in fighting, Israeli strikes and demolitions in southern Lebanon have continued.

At least 4,383 people - including 395 women and 259 children - have been killed in Lebanon by Israeli attacks since 2 March, according to the health ministry, whose figures do not differentiate between combatants and civilians. At least 29 have been killed this week, the ministry says.

Israeli authorities say 40 Israeli soldiers and four civilians have been killed in the same period.

Additional reporting by Raffi Berg in London and Samantha Granville and Ghaith Solh in Beirut

World.title: Norway's Princess Astrid dies two days after attending brother King Harald's funeral
World.content:
Princess Astrid of Norway, the sister of the late King Harald V, has died at the age of 94, two days after attending his funeral, the country's royal palace has announced.

The new king, Haakon VIII, said that "throughout her long life, Princess Astrid represented the Royal House in a warm and dutiful manner".

Harald died last month, aged 89, after more than 35 years as king. His funeral was Astrid's last public engagement.

The princess will be buried at state expense and flags will be flown at half-mast across Norway, Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re said.

Astrid was the last surviving child of King Olav V, who reigned from 1957 to 1991.

She became Norway's first lady at the age of 22 in 1954, after the death of her mother Crown Princess MÃ¤rtha. Olav did not remarry and Astrid retained the title until her brother's marriage in 1968.

"In her work, Princess Astrid was always particularly concerned with care and inclusion for the most vulnerable in society," her nephew King Haakon said in his statement.

Her health had deteriorated in recent months and in March she received hospital treatment for pneumonia.

Dozens of European royals and heads of state attended Harald's funeral on Wednesday, including the Prince of Wales and three Nordic kings.

Thousands of people lined the route during a procession from the royal palace to Oslo Cathedral on Wednesday afternoon.

The non-royal leaders paying their respects included Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and five foreign prime ministers.

World.title: Houthis claim major advance in Yemen and tighten grip on Red Sea shipping lane
World.content:
On Friday, Yemeni pro-government forces withdrew from Perim (also known as Mayyun).

Witnesses and news agencies reported that Houthi forces moved on to the island.

The Houthis later issued a statement, saying that their military operation to expel Saudi-backed forces had been a "success" and that "maritime navigation is safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels".

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said the "large-scale" military operation was launched on 3 September due to Saudi Arabia's "blatant aggression" against "our dear people".

Sarea also said the Houthis had expelled "Saudi enemy" forces from six districts in the Taiz and Hodeidah regions, claiming that hundreds of troops had been killed, wounded or captured.

The Houthi statement, however, did not mention Perim Island.

Saudi Arabia has not publicly commented on the latest developments.

Perim Island sits at the narrowest point of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which has become increasingly important following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz - another crucial waterway - in the conflict between the US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia has been relying on the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait for shipping oil to customers in Asia.

The escalation of the conflict between the Houthis, Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia has contributed to a surge in oil prices.

Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed and thousands displaced in Yemen since the Houthis launched an offensive in the south-west a week ago.

A Saudi-led coalition has also carried out air strikes on Houthi-controlled areas in western Yemen in support of the pro-government forces, and the Houthis have launched missiles and drones at cities and oil facilities in southern Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi foreign affairs ministry said on Friday that drones from Iraq had targeted the country's East-West oil pipeline, forcing it to be closed as a "precautionary measure" and injuring several people.

Iraq's government condemned the attack and its prime minister has launched an investigation.

In a statement, the prime minister's office said the operations commander in the Maysan governorate - a province which borders Iran - had been removed from his post following confirmation the drone attack had originated from that region.

Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said that, following a call from Iraq's prime minister, it had chosen not to respond to the attacks at this stage.

World.title: CAFCLQ: Rangers survive SOBEMAP scare as Rivers United await San Pedro test
World.content:
Rangers International have survived a nervy CAF Champions League preliminary-round tie against AS SOBEMAP of the Benin Republic, edging the Beninese champions 5-4 on penalties after another 1-1 draw in the second leg at Stade de Kégué, Lomé, on Friday.

The result saw the Flying Antelopes progress to the second preliminary round after the two sides finished level at 2-2 on aggregate, following identical 1-1 draws in both legs.

Rangers had entered the decisive encounter knowing that anything short of victory would put their continental campaign in danger after they were held to a frustrating draw in the first leg at their temporary home in Abeokuta.

The Nigerian champions once again found themselves involved in a tightly contested encounter in Lomé, with neither side able to produce the decisive goal during regulation time.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

With the aggregate score tied at 2-2, the contest had to be decided from the penalty spot.

Rangers showed greater composure when it mattered most, converting five of their penalties to edge the shootout 5-4 and book their place in the next round of Africa’s premier club competition.

The qualification will come as a major relief for the Flying Antelopes, who had been left frustrated after failing to capitalise on their chances in the first leg.

Chidozie Iwundu had scored Rangers’ goal in the opening encounter in Abeokuta, but AS SOBEMAP responded to ensure the tie remained evenly balanced heading into the return fixture.

Despite another difficult evening in Lomé, Rangers held their nerve in the shootout to avoid what would have been an early continental exit.

The Enugu club will now turn their attention to the second preliminary round, where they are set to face either the Niger Republic’s ASN Nigelec or Algerian giants MC Alger.

The two sides also played out a goalless draw in their first-leg meeting, leaving their own qualification battle finely poised ahead of the return fixture on Saturday.

For Rangers, Friday’s qualification represents an important step in their bid to reach the CAF Champions League group stage. Still, the challenge is set to become even tougher in the next round.

Rivers United still have work to do

While Rangers have secured their place in the next round, Nigeria’s other representative in the CAF Champions League, Rivers United, will have to wait until Sunday for their decisive second-leg encounter against FC San Pedro.

READ ALSO: Finidi eyes strong start as Rivers United begin Champions League campaign

The Port Harcourt club held San Pedro to a 1-1 draw in the first leg in Côte d’Ivoire, putting themselves in a promising position ahead of the return fixture at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo.

Rivers United will therefore know that victory on home soil will be enough to send them into the second preliminary round. At the same time, another draw would leave the tie requiring a further means of separation.

Finidi George’s side will be hoping to make home advantage count as they attempt to join Rangers in the next stage and strengthen Nigeria’s presence in the competition.

World.title: INTERVIEW: How we erroneously employed sodomy convict as lecturer – AUN President Dwayne Frazier
World.content:
In June, PREMIUM TIMES published a story that exposed how a former military officer, Bello Magaji, convicted of sodomy, avoided jail, got a pardon, and landed a job at the American University of Nigeria (AUN) in Yola, Adamawa State.

In this interview with our reporters – Qosim Suleiman, Ademola Popoola and Fareedah Bakare – the President of AUN, Dwayne Frazier, speaks on how the institution is handling the matter.

PT: PREMIUM TIMES recently published an expose about one of your staff members, Dr. Bello Magaji, who turned out to be someone who was convicted but never served his time. We would like to hear what was the thought of the university when that story came out?

Dwayne: Let me just point out that I just didn’t know. And then, to be able to find out exactly this, we jumped into action immediately. So, we did go on administrative leave, and then we’d have committees together because Nigeria is governed by the rule of law, just like the United States, third largest democracy in the world.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

So, we wanted to make sure everybody gets their fair say, their fair hearing. So, that’s ongoing. But we have made sure that he gets his fair say on why military experience was not placed on the resume and all these different things. And we’re going to do what’s fair.

PT: One of the famous questions we got after doing this story was how the university did not find this out? What did you find during your background check, and how did these facts slip by the checks?

Dwayne: He was hired before my administration. Different birthdays were written in there, and so that can get confusing. I didn’t realise, I wasn’t the one doing the background checks, and I also didn’t realise how unfortunate that people do put two different birthdates. So, it’s hard to tie people sometimes; even sending things to the military, other things that were out there that could have been falsified.

I’m not sure, but the biggest issue for most universities, and this is across the board at a macro level, is that people need to always place their complete work history on their application. You can’t just come back always and say, “Well, you know, that wasn’t relevant, this wasn’t important.” Let us make that determination if it was relevant.

You know, we might be having a different conversation if everybody knew everything from the beginning and said, ‘Well, this is not the right place for you, or this is the right place for you, but let’s do this and that.’ And then it wouldn’t have been such a surprise, because when things are a surprise to your employer and it makes them look like they were caught in the headlights in some way, that’s not good for anybody: not good for the candidate, it’s not good for the employee, it’s not good for the university or even the leadership. So, I say all of that in the most loving way I can, because the truth is everybody deserves their day in court.

PT: What exactly did the military tell you?

Dwayne: Once again, we’ve always had a great relationship with the military, so this is not me trying to say anything rude about them. But I think with the different birth date and then the picture where he’s aged, they could not identify that this was the same person that was in that rank. But as you probably already know, it’s hard when you get a letter that says that he was honourably discharged.

I would have never thought you would be honourably discharged, even if a presidential pardon came later and you got all the full benefits. And once again, I’m not a Nigerian, so I don’t always understand the nuances of that. But I know in the US that you wouldn’t be able to do that. So, all of it put me in a little bit of a surprise mode.

But once again, ultimately, that’s my fault. I shouldn’t be surprised. I’m learning as fast as I can. But the rest of my team has been very helpful, which includes many Nigerians and Americans.

But we’ve been able to make sure. And we’ve got great Governing Council members who understand law and other things. And they’ve been very instrumental in helping us. And it’s not about a public image or trying to protect yourself. If it’s about doing it right. That’s what matters to me.

PT: We asked Bello Magaji why he did not disclose this record to the university and his response was that the university never asked. Is that true?

Dwayne: That is not true because in the application, it’s very clear. Anybody who wants to apply for a job, and you’ll see it asks for your complete work history. You don’t just go back and say, I didn’t like that school.

Do you think if I didn’t include every university I worked for and be able to put the jobs that I was in, the firm in the United States that brought me here through the Board of Trustees, the largest academic search firm in the United States, would have hired me for this? They verified every credential; they called every school to see where I worked and if it was the right title. They wouldn’t have hired me if I left something out because they would think that you’re trying to hide something. And once again, I’m not saying he was trying to hide, but let’s keep in mind that when you omit something that’s over a decade-long service, it has to be relevant to what you’re doing.

I come from an Army family on one side, the US Army. They were based at Fort Knox, Kentucky, family in Heidelberg, Germany. The military teaches a lot about character and leadership, and teaches people how to work in systems.

And so that’s very relevant to being in an American university or any university. So, to say it’s not relevant and we didn’t ask- we did ask. It’s on the application. It’s in the materials. It doesn’t say, “Were you in the military? No. It says, all your work areas, and it asks all of those questions, you know, any criminal conviction.

I’m not a scholar of legality, but let’s remember that a presidential pardon in my country and in your country is important for the repercussions or the penalties that you get. But it does not reverse the fact that there was a conviction at that time. It just takes away all the penalties and everything. It doesn’t erase time.

Something happens in time. So, if I ask you today, have you ever been found guilty in a court? You can still put “I was pardoned”.

But you’re being disingenuous if you’re not telling me that happened. And I’m telling you, none of this did happen. And once again, I’ll step back again and just say, as a human being, as a person, during our time with him, he did do a good job. He’s not a mean person. He’s always been very helpful with me and everything.

But the rules are the rules, and integrity is integrity, and what’s right is what’s right, and we have to be honest with each other. So, even if that penalty has been taken away, it comes back to the committee and the group to look at: was it germane to him placing that there? And with the different birth dates and the other things, was that done to mislead us from that case? And if that’s the case, then that places us in a situation, that, we are in a law school, that is the people that are supposed to keep the law, so will that cause a challenge for people studying under someone, who quote and unquote might have obstructed the law.

PT: Just a day after our story was published, we were informed that the university suspended Dr Magaji indefinitely. It’s been close to a month now. Can you tell us how that suspension is going? Have there been some panels of inquiry, and what were the findings so far?

Dwayne: I can’t tell you exactly the findings, because it will be out pretty soon. But what I can tell you is the first group is all about substantiating what is said in the application, to give him his time. So, he was able to talk with them and share with the committee. The committee included some staff, faculty of the fellow rank, all of us.

We had our legal counsel, in-house legal counsel. So, we had a really good group. They listened to him, let him have his day and his conversation about why, and then they wrote up a report. And so whatever findings they come up with in that time period, there will be another group that can help me and advise me on what penalty, based upon our employee handbook and recommendation. And it would be before too long.

PT: Can you tell us what Dr Bello Magaji’s reaction was like when all of this came out and the university suspended him? Did he protest it? Was he just calm about it?

Dwayne: You know, he was actually calm. I told you I’ve never had any disagreement, fights, anything. He’s always been very, very kind to me and kind to other people, and very gentle. So, in that aspect, and I do point that out because this is not me trying to assassinate anyone’s character. Personally, he’s always been nice and kind to me. So, I judge people based on my interactions with them. But laws are laws, rules are rules, integrity is integrity.

But he didn’t. You know, when I first asked and said that PREMIUM TIMES said you are the same person, he said, “Yeah, I’m the same person, but I was pardoned.” So he was a little nonchalant, which was a little different to me, on something I felt was a pretty major situation. But he wasn’t rude. He wasn’t mad about it. He knew that he would follow the process and see where it goes. So, from that part, I have to say that I was happy about that because it wasn’t an easy thing to have a conversation with someone about this. But after that, he didn’t feel like he could talk to us, and I understand that, without legal counsel.

So, we’ll just go for these two months, or 30 to 60 days, and we’ll have that final decision. So, that’s completely in his right. Everybody has the right to be represented; even lawyers have the right to be represented from outside because of the emotions that could be involved when it involves us personally.

World.title: Oluremi Tinubu fulfills ₦10m pledge to 12-year-old Ogun artist
World.content:
Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, has fulfilled her ₦10 million education pledge to 12-year-old Ogun State artist, Master Morenikeji Ebunoluwa Joshua, less than a month after being impressed by his artistic talent.

The ₦10 million Education Development Trust Fund, presented to Joshua through the Ogun State Government, is to support his education through the tertiary level.

The First Lady had announced the pledge on August 18 after spotting Joshua displaying a portrait he had painted of her at the launch of the South-West Zonal National Food Bank Programme at the Cultural Centre, Kuto, Abeokuta.

Impressed by the quality of his work, Senator Tinubu invited the young artist to the podium and immediately pledged ₦10 million towards his future education.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Presenting the cheque on behalf of the First Lady, Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, described the fulfilment of the pledge as a demonstration that “a promise made is a promise kept.”

Abiodun said the gesture went beyond the financial value of the donation, describing it as an investment in a young Nigerian whose talent had been identified and encouraged.

He commended Joshua for his artistic ability and determination to showcase his work, urging other young people to identify, develop and promote their God-given talents.

“Young Joshua Morenikeji is someone who wants to be heard, he wants to be seen, he wants his talent to be appreciated, and that is a very strong virtue.

“The truth is that if you are not out there promoting yourself, nobody is likely to promote you,” the governor said.

The development also marked a continuation of government support for the young artist, with Abiodun recalling that he had personally intervened in Joshua’s education three years ago after seeing one of his paintings during an exhibition at his office.

According to the governor, further interaction with the young artist revealed that he was still in primary school, prompting him to provide a scholarship to take Joshua through primary and secondary education.

“I immediately announced a scholarship in his favour to see him through primary to secondary school, and that has been done,” he said.

With the latest intervention by Senator Tinubu, Joshua’s educational support has now been extended to the tertiary level.

Abiodun expressed appreciation to the First Lady for the gesture, describing her as a promise keeper and a strong supporter of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration.

He disclosed that an account had been opened specifically to ensure that the ₦10 million fund was preserved for Joshua’s educational needs.

“We extend our deepest appreciation for this gift of ₦10 million, whose account has been opened specifically for this purpose,” the governor said.

The governor also congratulated Joshua’s parents, urging them to continue supporting their son while encouraging the young artist to remain focused and further develop his talent.

Earlier, the Senior Special Assistant to the First Lady on Strategy, Wahab Alawiye-King, who handed over the cheque to Governor Abiodun, said Joshua’s story underscored the need for education to recognise and nurture different forms of talent.

She explained that education was not limited to academic performance but encompassed the cognitive, affective and psychomotor domains, covering intellectual development, values and emotions, as well as practical skills.

The Commissioner for Education, Science and Technology, Prof Abayomi Arigbabu, disclosed that the intervention was part of broader efforts to support deserving young people, revealing that 21 students from tertiary institutions had also received financial awards.

The beneficiaries comprised 14 students of Tai Solarin University of Education, six from Babcock University and one from Mountain Top University.

For Joshua, the intervention represents more than a reward for a portrait. It provides a pathway for him to pursue higher education while continuing to develop the artistic talent that brought him to national attention.

Speaking after receiving the support, Joshua thanked Senator Tinubu for recognising and investing in his talent, saying the gesture demonstrated that young talents could be seen, valued and encouraged.

He urged other children to identify their passions, pursue them diligently and continually work to improve their talents.

World.title: What NDC will do to protect votes in 2027 – Peter Obi’s ally
World.content:
Aisha Yesufu, an ally of the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, (NDC), Peter Obi, says the opposition will deploy a nationwide network of election agents in 2027 to monitor votes from polling units through the collation process to the final declaration in Abuja.

Mrs Yesufu said the strategy was informed by lessons from the 2023 presidential election, which she said showed that opposition supporters could not afford to rely solely on electoral institutions to protect their votes.

She spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday.

“We have our own alternative means of ensuring that we are protected,” Mrs Yesufu said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She said supporters would monitor election materials and results at every stage, from the polling unit to the ward and local government collation centres, state level and ultimately Abuja.

“There is no time that any ballot paper, any ballot box, result sheet or the individual will be out of our sight,” she said.

According to her, the movement would deploy people and resources to ensure that election materials are not diverted or altered during the collation process.

“We will follow them using bikes, we will follow them using boats, we will follow them by air,” she said, adding that supporters would continue monitoring the process until the results were entered and declared.

Mrs Yesufu said the objective was to ensure that the result declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reflected the votes cast at the polling units.

“We will ensure that no vote is changed from where it is voted and entered in to the place where the INEC chairman declares the final result,” she said.

‘We must take over every polling unit’

Ms Yesufu said the focus of the 2027 campaign would extend beyond rallies to the polling units, where she said the opposition intended to have a strong presence on election day.

“It’s not going to be at the rallies only. For me, my own is to be at the streets at every polling unit, that we must take over every polling unit and ensure that every vote is protected,” she said.

She said groups were already being organised around polling units as part of the preparation.

“At every polling unit, right, we have a council. We have at least nothing less than 20, 50, 100 depending on the polling units already mapping that out,” she said.

She said the structure would bring together supporters who were committed to participating in the election and protecting the votes cast for their candidates.

Mrs Yesufu said the experience of the 2023 election had reinforced the need for voters and political groups to take responsibility for protecting their ballots.

“The lesson from 2023 is that there’s no place of trusting the system or thinking that the institutions are going to do the right thing,” she said.

Mr Obi, the NDC presidential candidate, made a similar appeal to his supporters earlier in the week, urging them to defend their votes from the polling unit through to the final declaration of results.

‘We believe Obi won 2023’

Mrs Yesufu said she remained among those who believed that Mr Obi won the 2023 presidential election, despite the declaration of President Bola Tinubu as winner by INEC and the subsequent rejection of the challenge by the courts.

Mr Obi finished third in the 2023 election with 6.1 million votes, behind Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who scored 6.9 million, and Mr Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who won with 8.7 million votes.

Mr Obi and his supporters continue to claim that he won the election even though they could not prove how the former Anambra governor won the election.

Benue blockade

Mrs Yesufu also defended Mr Obi following the obstruction of his convoy in Benue State on Tuesday.

Mr Obi was travelling to Yelwata to commiserate with families affected by the 2025 attacks when his convoy was stopped by thugs on the Makurdi-Gboko federal highway. The police later said 46 suspects had been arrested in connection with the incident.

The Benue State Government denied involvement in the incident and said it was unaware of Mr Obi’s visit. The state government also said the visit should have been coordinated with relevant authorities.

Mrs Yesufu described Mr Obi as one of the most courageous politicians in Nigeria and said his decision not to force his way through the blockade was strategic.

“You need to understand something. There is a place where someone has to be strategic. You have a lot of things to do,” she said.

She said the incident reinforced the need for the opposition to remain organised as it prepares for the 2027 election.

The comments come as political parties and their candidates intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections, with the NDC placing greater emphasis on defending votes at polling units and through the results collation process.

World.title: Lawyer faults IGP’s comment, insists Nigerians have right to film police on duty
World.content:
Human rights lawyer Inibehe Effiong has faulted a recent comment by the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, that Nigerians should exercise restraint in filming police officers on duty.

The comment

On 17 March, the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State delivered a landmark judgement which affirmed Nigerians’ constitutional right to record police officers while they perform their duties in public.

During an interaction with the leadership of the Nigerian Bar Association in Abuja on Tuesday, Mr Disu said police operatives were “jostled” by the court judgement.

The IGP stressed that, in response to the judgement, Nigerians started recording police officers everywhere, including at restaurants.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This can be demoralising. Can we come to your offices and record you? Can we record even in the court? People coming to our offices with concealed cameras,” the IGP had said.

Lawyer fumes

While appearing as a guest on Channels TV’s The Morning Brief on Friday, Mr Effiong argued that Mr Disu’s complaints against filming of officers suggests that he might have been overwhelmed by cases of police misconduct confronting him.

The lawyer particularly faulted the IGP’s reference to anti-recording rule in Nigerian courtrooms.

He acknowledged that while it is true that filming proceedings in Nigerian courts was prohibited, it is not a situation to be proud of, especially considering that court proceedings are streamed live in Kenya, Uganda and other parts of Africa.

“So this is not something to be proud of. It is a challenge for the judiciary,” the lawyer said of the anti-filming rule in Nigerian courtrooms.

Mr Effiong clarified that while he supports calls to allow filming of court proceedings in Nigeria, such rule should not apply in all cases.

“So, the example that he (IGP) has cited is a false example. It’s a false equivalent. I do not agree with it,” he said.

The human rights lawyer then questioned the police’s concern about Nigerians filming officers on duty.

“Why do they have a problem with policemen being recorded while they are carrying out their functions? Are they scared of being shown that they are demanding bribes?

“Are they scared of being shown that they are torturing Nigerians? Are they scared of being shown that they are setting people’s backs?” he said.

Mr Effiong said contrary to the IGP’s claim, he had not seen evidence that Nigerians were filming police officers while they were eating.

“I haven’t seen that being a practice that is rampant on social media.

“So I would be happy if the police can cite some instances to portray the fact that the IGP has referenced,” he said, adding that the police chief appeared to be creating an imaginary problem.

The lawyer insisted that Nigerians have the constitutional right to record law enforcement officers while they were carrying out their responsibilities in public.

“But speaking generally, Nigerians have the right, unmistakably, to record incidents. Not just the police, but law enforcement officers generally, in the course of discharging their statutory responsibility,” he said.

He further contended that the 1999 Constitution as amended guarantees citizens rights to record officers, pointing out that even the Administration of Criminal Justice Act provides that obtaining a confessional statement from a suspect must be either in the presence of a legal practitioner of his choice, or on video record.

“So even the law is evolving to begin to accommodate that,” he said in reference to mobile devices used in recording.

Turning to Nigerians, he said: “I am encouraging Nigerians, please continue to record policemen who act unprofessionally because the courts have made it clear.”

World.title: Nigeria’s Seed Council, PIND partner to expand certified seed access
World.content:
Farmers across the Niger Delta are set to gain greater access to certified seeds and quality planting materials following a two-year partnership between the National Agricultural Seed Council (NASC) and the Foundation for Partnership Initiatives in the Niger Delta (PIND).

The organisations signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at NASC’s corporate headquarters in Abuja to expand community-based seed production, strengthen certification and inspection, develop local seed enterprises and mobilise investment in Nigeria’s domestic seed industry.

The partnership combines NASC’s regulatory and quality-assurance mandate with PIND’s market systems expertise and networks of Community Seed Entrepreneurs, Farm Service Providers, Business Service Providers, research institutions and private-sector partners.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, NASC Director-General, Fatuhu Muhammed, said the agreement would help bring quality-assurance services closer to farmers and seed producers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“A productive agricultural sector begins with quality seeds. By working with PIND and its networks across the Niger Delta, NASC can extend certification and inspection services to more communities, protect farmers from poor-quality planting materials and create stronger pathways for investment in Nigeria’s seed industry,” Mr Muhammed said.

PIND’s Executive Director, Sam Daibo, said the partnership would help move proven community-level interventions to institutional adoption and scale.

“Many farmers understand the value of quality seeds but cannot access certified planting materials when and where they need them. By combining NASC’s regulatory leadership with PIND’s market systems experience, we can close that gap, strengthen local seed enterprises and help farmers build more productive and commercially viable livelihoods,” Mr Daibo said.

From cassava to other crops

The MoU formalises a collaboration dating back to 2016 through the Building an Economically Sustainable Seed System for Cassava programme, implemented in partnership with the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) and the National Root Crops Research Institute (NRCRI).

The collaboration later expanded into community-based cassava seed multiplication, with NASC certifying seed plots across the Niger Delta.

Under the new framework, NASC and PIND will expand NASC-certified community seed multiplication across the region.

NASC will lead certification and quality assurance, while PIND will support enterprise development, technical assistance and market linkages.

According to the statement, the partners will also extend NASC’s Licensed Seed Inspectors Scheme into the Niger Delta, drawing potential candidates from PIND’s Farm Service Provider and Business Service Provider networks.

The partnership will further promote domestic seed production for high-demand vegetables, including tomato, pepper and cucumber, while expanding access to cassava, banana and yam planting materials produced through NASC’s PROSSIVA programme, the statement said.

It said the agreement will also support the Mastercard Foundation-funded WISE programme by enabling NASC to certify Community Seed Entrepreneurs trained to supply quality cassava planting materials to women producers across the Niger Delta.

ALSO READ: NBMA disposes of 950kg of unapproved GM cotton seeds

The partnership’s first major joint deliverable will be the Nigeria Seed Systems Forum 2026 in Abuja.

The forum is expected to bring together policymakers, regulators, researchers, investors, seed companies, development partners and farmers to advance policy, investment and market action in Nigeria’s seed sector.

A Joint Technical Working Group comprising representatives of NASC and PIND will coordinate implementation and track progress under the agreement.

Through the partnership, the organisations aim to strengthen the connection between regulation, research, enterprise development and markets, bringing certified seeds closer to farmers while supporting a stronger and more commercially sustainable seed industry in Nigeria.

World.title: Bandits kill four police officers, seven civilians in Benue attack
World.content:
Four police officers and seven civilians were killed when suspected armed bandits attacked Ayilamo community in Logo Local Government Area of Benue State, the police have confirmed.

The attack occurred on Thursday evening and lasted about seven hours before the attackers were repelled and fled into the surrounding forest, the Benue State Police Command said.

The command said the attackers invaded the community at about 6:12 p.m. on 10 September.

Officers from the Police Mobile Force, tactical teams and conventional police engaged the assailants in a sustained gun battle, according to a statement issued on Friday by the command’s spokesperson, Orchia Aondongu.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The operatives stood firm in defence of the community and successfully repelled the attack, forcing the criminal elements to retreat into the surrounding forest with heavy casualties in the early hours of 11th September 2026,” Mr Aondongu said.

But four police officers were killed during the operation.

The command identified them as Paul Ina, Mohammed Yusuf, Oge Ikechukwu and Edeh Andrew.

Their bodies were recovered from surrounding bushes during search and rescue operations, the police said.

Seven civilians were also killed. Their bodies were recovered after the attack and deposited at a mortuary, according to the command.

Residents recount attack

A resident, Tyolumun Ugande, told journalists that about 200 suspected armed herders invaded the community, shooting at residents and burning houses.

He said Mobile Police officers deployed to Ayilamo confronted the attackers.

“A detachment of Mobile Policemen deployed to Ayilamo confronted the bandits who were armed with sophisticated weapons,” Mr Ugande said.

“After several hours of exchange of gunfire, the bandits retreated but on Friday morning four bodies of Mobile Policemen and residents of the community were recovered in the bush.”

The Secretary of the Ayilamo Security Committee, Umishi Terungwa, also confirmed the attack.

Mr Terungwa said the attack occurred between Thursday night and the early hours of Friday and described the victims as including community elders, residents and security personnel.

He identified some of the civilian victims as Nyikyaa Agia, Mkohol Ahowe, Agah Saanmoyol, popularly known as Dodo, Mlahaga Kpurkpur, Geoffrey Gaku, also known as Bala, and two children.

Mr Ugande had initially put the death toll at 12, including four police officers and eight civilians. The police later confirmed 11 deaths, comprising four officers and seven civilians.

Ayilamo division created amid security concerns

The latest attack comes about a year after the police upgraded the Ayilamo Police Station to a divisional headquarters as part of a broader restructuring of policing in Benue.

On 20 August 2025, the then Benue Police Public Relations Officer, Udeme Edet, announced that Inspector-General of Police Kayode Egbetokun had approved the creation of two new area commands and upgraded five police stations to divisional status.

Ayilamo was among the five stations upgraded.

The other stations were Yelewata, Jato-Aka, Okpokolo and Agan.

The police said at the time that the restructuring followed an assessment that identified “geographical gaps” between police formations and vulnerable communities in troubled parts of the state.

The newly created Daudu Area Command was to oversee Guma, Daudu, Yelwata and Agan divisions, while Naka Area Command was to supervise Naka, Apa, Agatu and Okpokolo divisions.

Ms Edet said the restructuring was intended to improve police response in areas with difficult terrain and facilitate the resolution of farmer-herder conflicts and distress calls.

“This adjustment will assist the command in policing troubled areas with large and difficult terrains. These Divisions will also ensure quick resolution of conflict between farmers and herders and facilitate quick response to distress calls,” she said.

ALSO READ: Suspected herders kill 14 in another Benue attack

The then Commissioner of Police in Benue, Ifeanyi Emenari, described the restructuring as a “crucial intervention” aimed at strengthening policing in the state.

But the killing of four police officers and seven civilians in Ayilamo less than two years after the division was created highlights the continuing security challenges confronting communities in the area.

Additional police deployed

Following Thursday’s attack, the police said additional tactical teams had been mobilised and deployed to Ayilamo to reinforce existing security arrangements.

The command said it was also working with other security agencies to strengthen security and sustain operations in the affected area.

The Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, commended the officers who responded to the attack and paid tribute to the four officers killed.

He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased civilians and the Ayilamo community.

The command urged residents to remain calm and vigilant and to provide timely information that could assist security agencies in their ongoing operations.

World.title: Gov Lawal supports Zamfara higher institutions with official vehicles
World.content:
Governor Dauda Lawal has distributed official vehicles to higher institutions to strengthen the capacity, efficiency, and effectiveness of Zamfara State’s education system.

The distribution of the official vehicles was held on Friday at the Government House in Gusau, the state capital.

A statement by the Governor’s Spokesperson, Sulaiman Bala Idris, said the vehicles are institutional assets and operational tools to support administration, supervision, accreditation, official engagements, and other legitimate responsibilities of the benefiting institutions.

The statement noted that institutions and offices allocated brand-new vehicles are Federal University Gusau, Zamfara State University, Talata Mafara, and Abdu Gusau Polytechnic, Talata Mafara.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Other beneficiaries are the College of Nursing and Midwifery, Gusau; the Teachers Service Board; the Senior Secondary School Board; Quality Assurance; ZACAS; and other State Government Public Institutions.

In his remarks, Governor Lawal reiterated that the initiative will increase the productivity of Zamfara State public office holders by providing reliable transportation, enabling them to deliver services more effectively and quickly.

He said, “It is important to emphasise that these vehicles are not personal entitlements for any office holder. They remain the property of the Zamfara State Government and must be used responsibly and strictly for official purposes.

“I expect institutions to be responsible for custody, deployment, maintenance, and documentation. Heads will be accountable for misuse, unauthorised use, or unnecessary deterioration of assets.

“As the government invests in education, we must foster a culture of maintenance and accountability. Public assets should provide value throughout their life. We must commit to higher standards of service, emphasising transparency and accountability.

“Our administration will continue to provide the infrastructure, equipment, and institutional support needed to improve higher education in Zamfara State. In return, we expect responsible leadership, prudent management, and measurable improvements in academic and administrative performance.”

Governor Lawal further congratulated the benefiting institutions and urged them to ensure that the vehicles serve the institutions, students, and the people of Zamfara State rather than individual interests.

World.title: Lady Gaga welcomes first child
World.content:
File: Lady Gaga and Michael Polansky. Photo by Alberto PIZZOLI / AFP.

Pop superstar Lady Gaga welcomed her first child with fiance Michael Polansky, US media reported Friday.

The 40-year-old “Bad Romance” singer, whose real name is Stefani Germanotta, began dating Polansky in 2020, and became engaged to the entrepreneur in 2024.

A source confirmed news of the child’s birth to Page Six and People, but no additional details about the baby, including its name, sex or date of birth, were immediately available.

The musician affectionately referred to as “Mother Monster” by her fans has spoken in recent years about her desire to have a child.

She wrapped up her most recent world tour, the Mayhem Ball, in April, and her latest album “Mayhem” garnered multiple Grammy nominations, winning the award for “Best Pop Vocal Album” earlier this year.
